How a session works

Three steps, about ten minutes

  1. Pick the call. Choose a scenario and how the other person behaves, or type your own: last week's call, a specific driver, a specific auditor.
  2. Run it out loud. You are the officer. The other person reacts to what you actually say: calm and specific settles things, sarcasm and vague orders escalate them.
  3. Get graded. A scorecard names the moment most likely to end up on bodycam or in a lawsuit, with the exact words to use instead.

Four officer-side scenarios

What each one tests

Traffic stopA nervous driver, an argumentative one, a "traveling, not driving" sovereign citizen, a possibly impaired driver, or one who declares a firearm. Scored on procedure and lawful basis, safety, communication and composure.Crisis de-escalationA mental-health crisis, an agitated man refusing to leave, a hostile drunk, a domestic aftermath, or someone in despair. Scored on safety, tone, listening and outcome. Kept non-graphic.First Amendment auditAn auditor films you in the lobby, from the sidewalk or near a scene, politely or to bait you. Scored on lawful basis, composure, clarity and resolution.Courtroom testimonyA defense attorney cross-examines you on your own report and hunts for the gap. Scored on accuracy, discipline, composure and credibility.

For departments and training units

  • $15 per officer a month, 300 rounds each, 3-seat minimum. Annual invoicing is available for departments that need a purchase order; ask us.
  • Supervisors see scores, never transcripts: sessions, average scores, and the department's weakest skills over the last 30 days.
  • Trainers can write their own scenarios. Describe the driver, the call or the auditor in plain language and every officer runs the same scenario.
  • Audio is never stored. Sessions are kept as text so officers can review their own scorecards.
  • Training practice, not legal advice. Follow your department's policy and state law. We recommend departments treat the scorecards as practice feedback, not as training records, until a department confirms what its academy accepts.

FAQ

Questions, answered

How do departments buy?

Create a team or department from the Account page after signing up, invite officers with a link, and pay per seat. For purchase orders or an annual invoice, write to support@getadversaryai.com.

Is this approved training?

It is practice. We do not claim POST or academy credit. Some departments file the completion records internally; check with your training unit.

Does it handle realistic calls without refusing?

Yes. The content filtering is tuned for realistic police scenarios, including crisis calls and weapons, while keeping everything non-graphic.

Is there a version for the public?

Yes: Know Your Rights lets a citizen rehearse a traffic stop or street encounter calmly. It is a separate mode.

What does it cost?

Your first 15 rounds are free with no card. After that: Debater is $12 a month for 300 rounds, Coach is $29 for 750, Champion is $49 for 500 premium rounds plus 60 minutes of photoreal video opponents, and Elite is $100 for 1,000 premium rounds and 2 hours of video. Round packs are $9 for 100, $19 for 250 and $39 for 600, and pack rounds never expire. Teams and departments pay $15 per seat a month, schools $6.
